plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, overbidding risks paying more than my value warrants, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit no matter the strategies of Betty and Charles, since the mechanism is incentive-compatible. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $30.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do or think about your strategy. This holds because if you bid your value, you win exactly when the prize is worth more to you than the price you'd pay (the second-highest bid), maximizing expected profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than your value; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With value $7, I should bid exactly $7.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders, where bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, there's no incentive to shade my bid below or above my true valuation of $36. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
